title: ChaosForge-Lab
description: Predictable chaos engineering tool for testing Kubernetes auto-healing and Terraform recovery with live metrics.
details: Leveraged Kubernetes configurations and AWS Fault Injection Simulator to randomly terminate pods and EC2 nodes. Proved the architecture's self-healing capabilities and significantly reduced recovery time objective (RTO) during simulated outages.

title: GitOps EKS Cluster Provisioning
description: Automated the deployment of an AWS EKS cluster using Terraform, with ArgoCD managing continuous deployment of microservices.
details: Implemented a fully declarative GitOps workflow. Terraform provisions the VPC and EKS cluster, while ArgoCD constantly reconciles the live cluster state against the GitHub repository. This eliminates configuration drift and enables 1-click disaster recovery.

title: Serverless Log Analytics Pipeline
description: Built an event-driven architecture using Python (Boto3) and AWS Lambda to parse CloudWatch logs and trigger SNS alerts for anomalies.
details: Designed a cost-effective, event-driven monitoring solution. AWS Lambda functions parse CloudWatch logs in real-time, matching specific error patterns and routing critical alerts to SNS topics. Effectively reduced alert fatigue by filtering noise.

title: Highly Available 3-Tier VPC Design
description: Architected a fault-tolerant AWS environment spanning multiple Availability Zones with Application Load Balancers and Auto Scaling Groups.
details: Built a production-ready AWS network topology from scratch. Features public and private subnets across 3 Availability Zones, NAT Gateways for secure outbound traffic, and an Application Load Balancer distributing traffic to an Auto Scaling Group.

title: GitOps-Backed React Portfolio
description: A modular, Git-backed React portfolio automatically deployed via GitHub Actions. Features a custom headless CMS.
details: Instead of a simple static site, I engineered a serverless headless CMS. React handles the frontend, Tailwind manages the responsive UI, and GitHub Actions automatically builds and deploys changes to GitHub Pages whenever I push a new Markdown post via the GitHub API.
